newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen stronger next week.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen stronger next week.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.27 percent on Friday with participants reluctant to take up fresh positions ahead of a long weekend.
Traders said prices could firm as soon as next week due to lower bank deposit interest rates, which will be reduced by about 1.5 percent from April 1.
"Because of lower deposit interest rates some domestic investors may decide to move money into shares," said Mateja Gubanec, a trader at bank A banka.

"Although shares will not grow to their February levels, the index could gain another 200 points by the end of the year as the growing trend is expected to be sustained by foreign investors that are expected to resume buying in the next month or two," an analyst said.
The SBI index fell 3.43 points to 1,274.26.
Food company Kolinska had the highest turnover, down 4.19 percent to 2,010 tolars on volume of 12,123 shares.
Overall eight shares fell, six rose, one was unchanged and 11 were untraded. Turnover firmed to 80.6 million tolars from 50.4 million.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, down 17.48 percent to 12,750 tolars on volume of one share only.
Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading gainer, closing five percent higher at 12,600 on volume of eight shares.
The Ljubljana Stock Exchange will be closed for Easter on Monday. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
